thesis: Casino-style use is a configuration with vague value and stopping criteria, not an identity of LLMs.

ideas.statement: Control of formulation, selection and acceptance can turn repetition into tested exploration.
Ask what became demonstrable, built or understood instead of only what remains promising.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: At first glance, the comparison is almost too easy. You put something in, wait, and an outcome of uncertain value appears. When the outcome does not satisfy you, you repeat. But a good analogy must not win by eliminating the differences.

With an LLM, you can change the problem, the data, the instructions, and the evaluation criteria. You can request an executed calculation, a verifiable source, or a comparison with an example. In many activities, these interventions genuinely matter. Describing the entire process as pressing a button with no influence on the result would be false.

A language model operates with distributions conditioned on context; it does not draw words uniformly from a bag. The decoding strategy influences the diversity and coherence of the result. Research by Holtzman and colleagues explored precisely the differences between generation strategies and their effects on text. It does not follow that less randomness automatically produces truth. [6]

For readers who do not program, the distinction can be put this way: an answer can be the most natural one in a particular context and still be wrong about the world. What fits an explanation and what an observation confirms are not identical criteria.

Moreover, an agent is not merely the model. It can include tools, memory, file access, an execution environment, and acceptance rules. A model that assumes the result of a calculation and a system that executes it do not provide the same evidence. This book will use “LLM” for the model and “agent” for a system that can organize and perform actions, without assuming its autonomy is unlimited.

There are at least three forms of control in this relationship. Control over formulation: what question I ask and what context I provide. Control over selection: which version I choose and why. Control over acceptance: what must be demonstrated before the result produces effects.

The last form often receives less attention than the first. We discuss how to formulate the perfect request at length, and the conditions under which we would reject an impeccably written answer less often. But a system that lets users request anything without helping them verify anything offers incomplete freedom.

A simple example: we request a summary of a fictional two-page contract. We can ask for it to be “clearer” ten times. Or we can stipulate that every obligation mentioned must be linked to its corresponding paragraph, and that omitted obligations must be sought separately. The second strategy does not guarantee a perfect interpretation, but it changes the process: from choosing an agreeable text to checking verifiable relationships.

Some research methods deliberately use multiple generations. Wang and colleagues showed that aggregating different solution paths can improve performance on certain reasoning tasks. The finding justifies controlled exploration; it does not justify assuming that any majority of answers is true or that repetitions are independent. [7]

A programmer can generate several implementations and subject them to the same independent test suite. A writer can explore rhythms and voices. A researcher can request alternative hypotheses and then check their predictions. In such cases, variety serves a selection process.

Repetition becomes harder to defend when the only criterion is immediate satisfaction and the task requires truth. Regenerating a conclusion until it matches what you hoped for is not the same as verifying it. It can be an elaborate way to formulate your own preferred answer.

We will therefore use the expression “casino-style mode of use,” not the label “LLM equals slot machine.” In this mode, the value of the result is unstable or hard to assess, continuation is fueled by the intermittent appearance of impressive results, and the stopping criterion remains vague.

This is an operational description proposed in the book, not a medical category. A session can pass through it temporarily without significant consequences. Moreover, free exploration can deliberately lack a final objective. Playing with possibilities needs no apology.

But when we claim to be working, discovering, or deciding for others, we must add a question: after an hour, what has changed in what we can demonstrate, build, or understand? If the only answer is that the next hour looks promising, it is worth checking who is running the session.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Generations need not be independent, free play is legitimate and the proposed mode is not medical.

audit.notes: Complete chapter read; preserve proposed concepts, empirical limits and non-diagnostic distinctions.
